counterfactual_missing_items: More detailed histopathological findings unique to lupus erythematosus
Laboratory results showing elevated inflammatory markers
decisive_items: Dense lymphoplasmacellular infiltrate in the dermis, with scattered neutrophils and eosinophils
Granular and linear deposition of IgG and C3 at the basement membrane zone and abundant intercellular deposition of IgG and C3 in the upper two-thirds of the epidermis
response.rationale: R3 is the champion due to its strong support from laboratory tests and histopathological findings, which are consistent with lupus erythematosus. C1 is the runner-up as it shares some similarities with R3 but lacks the comprehensive support from various diagnostic modalities.

rejected.why: Lack of direct support from laboratory tests and histopathological findings
Insufficient evidence to support pemphigus as the primary diagnosis
